purpose: Cut bounded subtractive features directly into observed existing rigid static UC GLB rectangular-prism meshes, including rotated stock and hash-linked cumulative fabrication chains that recompile prior state before appending another verified cut.

properties.source_path: existing ordinary .glb creation outside protected live machine body
properties.path: distinct target .glb path outside protected live machine body
properties.specification: closed v0.2 axis-aligned cut recipe, v0.3 oriented cut recipe, or axm.mesh-fabrication-chain/v0.4 cumulative box-notch recipe
properties.expected_source_sha256: optional exact lowercase SHA-256 binding, with optional sha256: prefix
properties.lineage_path: v0.4 optional prior fabrication-lineage JSON receipt when appending to a previous chain output
properties.receipt_path: v0.4 optional distinct output JSON receipt path; defaults beside the output GLB
properties.expected_lineage_sha256: v0.4 optional exact prior lineage SHA-256 binding

contains: exact source GLB SHA-256 and source byte count
source closed edge-topology evidence before initial cutting
right-handed orthonormal source-frame axes and frame digest for rotated stock
cut recipe digests bound to exact source/frame state
v0.4 hash-linked cumulative cut/step lineage and final receipt digest
v0.4 deterministic reconstruction of the prior cumulative output before any resume append
kerf-aware cut metrics and cumulative cut count
output closed edge-topology evidence before publication

relationships: reads actual existing GLB triangles through UC's static geometry decoder before calculating the first cut
reuses UC seam-weld topology evidence before and after fabrication
derives an orthonormal local frame from the observed eight stock corners instead of assuming world-axis alignment
binds an explicit world-space fabrication axis to exactly one proven source-frame axis
v0.4 preserves that proven source frame as lineage instead of relaxing rectangular-stock recognition after the first subtraction
v0.4 verifies prior receipt hashes, prior output digest and deterministic prior-output reconstruction before appending new cuts
v0.4 builds cumulative non-overlapping box notches from the proven original stock state and emits a new append-only receipt
reuses the existing deterministic surface-to-GLB publisher and validator
keeps source bytes separate from the new output and refuses in-place cutting
limitations: v0.4 cumulative chaining is bounded to at most 32 non-overlapping/non-touching box-notch cuts on one proven fabrication axis of one rigid rectangular-prism root stock. Round-hole chaining and cross-axis chains remain unavailable.
v0.3 single cuts still support round through-holes and box notches on rotated/transformed rectangular stock; arbitrary free-angle cutters relative to the proven stock frame remain rejected.
Multiple primitives/components, skins, animation, morphs, UVs, textures, tangents, vertex colours, joints and unsupported material state remain rejected rather than silently discarded.

A v0.4 lineage receipt is content-hashed and exact-output-bound, but it is not a cryptographic authorship signature or an external trust anchor against a coordinated rewrite of both receipt and artifact.

General arbitrary-mesh boolean surgery remains unavailable. Edge-manifold topology is checked, but self-intersection, visual quality, structural strength, real manufacturing behavior and host-engine import are not proven.

truth.basis: Exact source bytes, source frame, cumulative cut recipes, parent/child step hashes, deterministic prior-output reconstruction, output topology, output digest, receipt digest and unsupported boundaries remain inspectable.

agency.basis: The caller chooses source, output, fabrication axis, cut locations/dimensions/kerf, resume receipt and replacement decision; the machine refuses unsupported overlap, cross-axis and freeform requests instead of inventing geometry.

continuity.basis: Source artifacts are read-only, resume receipts are append-only, prior output is deterministically reconstructed before continuation, in-place mutation is rejected and output/receipt publication retains rollback behavior.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: The cutter proves initial stock topology/frame, validates every lineage hash and exact prior output on resume, rejects overlapping cumulative cuts, then proves closed output topology and published GLB structure before claiming a validated chain.
